entries.475170d22c657779634a98bea0b279579b06bd0a: <div sID="gen19263" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="45" osisID="Ezek.45" sID="Ezek.45"/> <div eID="gen19263" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19264" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen19265" type="x-p"/> In this chapter is further represented to the prophet, in vision, I. The division of the holy land, so much for the temple, and the priests that attended the service of it (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.1-Ezek.45.4">ver. 1-4</reference>), so much for the Levites (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.5">ver. 5</reference>), so much for the city (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.6">ver. 6</reference>), so much for the prince, and the residue to the people, <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.7-Ezek.45.8">ver. 7, 8</reference>. II. The ordinances of justice that were given both to prince and people, <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.9-Ezek.45.12">ver. 9-12</reference>. III. The oblations they were to offer, and the prince's part in those oblations, <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.13-Ezek.45.17">ver. 13-17</reference>. Particularly in the beginning of the year (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.18-Ezek.45.20">ver. 18-20</reference>) and in the passover, and the feast of tabernacles, <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.21-Ezek.45.25">ver. 21-25</reference>. And all this seems to point at the new church-state that should be set up under the gospel, which, both for extent and for purity, should far exceed that of the Old Testament.
entries.c72265c46a5590925900b5455e0c5c8bdcc3cfb8: <div eID="gen19265" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen19264" type="introduction"/> <title type="x-s3">The Division of the Holy Land. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 574.)</title> <div sID="gen19266" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> Moreover, when ye shall divide by lot the land for inheritance, ye shall offer an oblation unto the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , a holy portion of the land: the length <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> the length of five and twenty thousand <hi type="italic">reeds,</hi> and the breadth <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> ten thousand. This <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> holy in all the borders thereof round about. <hi type="super">2</hi> Of this there shall be for the sanctuary five hundred <hi type="italic">in length,</hi> with five hundred <hi type="italic">in breadth,</hi> square round about; and fifty cubits round about for the suburbs thereof. <hi type="super">3</hi> And of this measure shalt thou measure the length of five and twenty thousand, and the breadth of ten thousand: and in it shall be the sanctuary <hi type="italic">and</hi> the most holy <hi type="italic">place.</hi> <hi type="super">4</hi> The holy <hi type="italic">portion</hi> of the land shall be for the priests the ministers of the sanctuary, which shall come near to minister unto the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> : and it shall be a place for their houses, and an holy place for the sanctuary. <hi type="super">5</hi> And the five and twenty thousand of length, and the ten thousand of breadth, shall also the Levites, the ministers of the house, have for themselves, for a possession for twenty chambers. <hi type="super">6</hi> And ye shall appoint the possession of the city five thousand broad, and five and twenty thousand long, over against the oblation of the holy <hi type="italic">portion:</hi> it shall be for the whole house of Israel. <hi type="super">7</hi> And a <hi type="italic">portion shall be</hi> for the prince on the one side and on the other side of the oblation of the holy <hi type="italic">portion,</hi> and of the possession of the city, before the oblation of the holy <hi type="italic">portion,</hi> and before the possession of the city, from the west side westward, and from the east side eastward: and the length <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> over against one of the portions, from the west border unto the east border. <hi type="super">8</hi> In the land shall be his possession in Israel: and my princes shall no more oppress my people; and <hi type="italic">the rest of</hi> the land shall they give to the house of Israel according to their tribes. <div eID="gen19266" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19267" type="x-p"/> Directions are here given for the dividing of the land after their return to it; and, God having warranted them to do it, would be an act of faith, and not of folly, thus to divide it before they had it. And it would be welcome news to the captives to hear that they should not only return to their own land, but that, whereas they were now but few in number, they should <hi type="italic">increase and multiply,</hi> so as to <hi type="italic">replenish</hi> it. But this never had its accomplishment in the Jewish state after the return out of captivity, but was to be fulfilled in the model of the Christian church, which was perfectly new (as this division of the land was quite different from that in Joshua's time) and much enlarged by the accession of the Gentiles to it; and it will be perfected in the heavenly kingdom, of which the land of Canaan had always been a type. Now, 1. Here is the portion of land assigned to <hi type="italic">the sanctuary,</hi> in the midst of which the temple was to be built, with all its courts and purlieus; the rest round about it was for the priests. This is called (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.1">v. 1</reference>) <hi type="italic">an oblation to the Lord;</hi> for what is given in works of piety, for the maintenance and support of the worship of God and the advancement of religion, God accepts as given to him, if it be done with a single eye. It is a <hi type="italic">holy portion of the land,</hi> which is to be set out first, as the <hi type="italic">first-fruits</hi> that sanctify the lump. The appropriating of lands for the support of religion and the ministry is an act of piety that bids as fair for perpetuity, and the benefit of posterity, as any. This <hi type="italic">holy portion of the land</hi> was to be measured, and the borders of it fixed, that the sanctuary itself might not have more than its share and in time engross the whole land. So far the lands of the church shall extend and no further; as in our own kingdom donations to the church were of old limited by the <hi type="italic">statute of mortmain.</hi> The lands here allotted to the sanctuary were 25,000 <hi type="italic">reeds</hi> (so our translation makes it, though some make them only <hi type="italic">cubits</hi>) in length, and 10,000 in breadth-about eighty miles one way and thirty miles another way (say some); twenty-five miles one way and ten miles the other way, so others. The priests and Levites that were to come near to minister were to have their dwellings in this <hi type="italic">portion of the land</hi> that was round about the sanctuary, that they might be near their work; whereas by the distribution of land in Joshua's time the cities of the priests and Levites were dispersed all the nation over. This intimates that gospel ministers should reside upon their charge; where their service lies there must they live. 2. Next to the lands of the sanctuary the city-lands are assigned, in which the holy city was to be built, and with the issues and profits of which the citizens were to be maintained (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.6">v. 6</reference>): <hi type="italic">It shall be for the whole house of Israel,</hi> not appropriated, as before, to one tribe or two, but some of all the tribes shall dwell in the city, as we find they did, <reference osisRef="Neh.11.1-Neh.11.2">Neh. xi. 1, 2</reference>. The portion for the city was fully as long, but only half as broad, as that for the sanctuary; for the city was enriched by trade and therefore had the less need of lands. 3. The next allotment after the church-lands and the city-lands is of the crown-lands, <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.7-Ezek.45.8">v. 7, 8</reference>. Here is no admeasurement of these, but they are said to lie <hi type="italic">on the one side and on the other side</hi> of the church-lands and city-lands, to intimate that the prince with his wealth and power was to be a protection to both. Some make the prince's share equal to the church's and city's share both together; others make it to be a thirteenth part of the rest of the land, the other twelve parts being for the twelve tribes. The prince that attends continually to the administration of public affairs must have wherewithal to support his dignity, and have abundance, that he may not be in temptation to oppress the people, which yet with many does not prevent that; but the grace of God shall prevent it, for it is promised here, <hi type="italic">My princes shall no more oppress my people;</hi> for God will make the <hi type="italic">officers peace</hi> and the <hi type="italic">exactors righteousness.</hi> Notwithstanding this, we find that after the return of the Jews to their own land the princes were complained of for their exactions. But Nehemiah was one that did not do as the <hi type="italic">former governors,</hi> and yet kept a handsome court, <reference osisRef="Neh.5.15">Neh. v. 15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Neh.5.18">18</reference>. But so much is said of the prince in this mystical holy state, to intimate that in the gospel-church magistrates should be as <hi type="italic">nursing fathers</hi> to it and Christian princes its patrons and protectors; and the holy religion they profess, as far as they are subject to the power of it, will restrain them from oppressing God's people, because they are more his people than theirs. 4. The rest of the lands were to be distributed to the people <hi type="italic">according to their tribes,</hi> who had reason to think themselves well settled, when they had both the <hi type="italic">testimony of Israel</hi> and the <hi type="italic">throne of judgment</hi> so near them.
entries.a7b3544c19a9e926618db4388530bae5227e377f: <div eID="gen19267" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">Rules of Justice. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 574.)</title> <div sID="gen19268" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">9</hi> Thus saith the Lord <hi type="small-caps">God</hi> ; Let it suffice you, O princes of Israel: remove violence and spoil, and execute judgment and justice, take away your exactions from my people, saith the Lord <hi type="small-caps">God</hi> . <hi type="super">10</hi> Ye shall have just balances, and a just ephah, and a just bath. <hi type="super">11</hi> The ephah and the bath shall be of one measure, that the bath may contain the tenth part of a homer, and the ephah the tenth part of a homer: the measure thereof shall be after the homer. <hi type="super">12</hi> And the shekel <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> twenty gerahs: twenty shekels, five and twenty shekels, fifteen shekels, shall be your maneh. <div eID="gen19268" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19269" type="x-p"/> We have here some general rules of justice laid down both for prince and people, the rules of distributive and commutative justice; for godliness without honesty is but a form of godliness, will neither please God nor avail to the benefit of any people. Be it therefore enacted, by the authority of the church's King and God, 1. That <hi type="italic">princes do not oppress their subjects,</hi> but duly and faithfully administer justice among them (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.9">v. 9</reference>): "<hi type="italic">Let it suffice you, O princes of Israel!</hi> that you have been oppressive to the people and have enriched yourselves by spoil and violence, that you have so long fleeced the flock instead of feeding them, and henceforward do so no more." Note, Even princes and great men that have long done amiss must at length think it time, high time, to reform and amend; for no prescription will justify a wrong. Instead of saying that they have been long accustomed to oppress, and therefore may persist in it, for the custom will bear them out, they should say that they have been long accustomed to it and therefore, as here, <hi type="italic">Let the time pass suffice,</hi> and let them now remove <hi type="italic">violence and spoil;</hi> let them drop wrongful demands, cancel wrongful usages, and turn out those from employments under them that do violence. Let them <hi type="italic">take away their exactions,</hi> ease their subjects of those taxes which they find lie heavily upon them, and let them <hi type="italic">execute judgment and justice</hi> according to the law, as the duty of their place requires. Note, All princes, but especially the princes of Israel, are concerned to do justice; for of their people God says, They are my people, and they in a special manner <hi type="italic">rule for God.</hi> 2. That one neighbour do not cheat another in commerce (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.10">v. 10</reference>): <hi type="italic">You shall have just balances,</hi> in which to weigh both money and goods, a <hi type="italic">just ephah</hi> for dry measure of corn and flour, a <hi type="italic">just bath</hi> for the measure of liquids, wine, and oil; and the <hi type="italic">ephah</hi> and <hi type="italic">bath</hi> shall be <hi type="italic">one measure,</hi> the tenth part of a <hi type="italic">chomer,</hi> or <hi type="italic">cor,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.11">v. 11</reference>. So that the ephah and bath contained (as the learned Dr. Cumberland has computed) seven wine gallons and four pints, and something more. An omer was but the tenth part of an ephah (<reference osisRef="Exod.16.36">Exod. xvi. 36</reference>) and the one hundredth part of a <hi type="italic">chomer,</hi> or <hi type="italic">homer,</hi> and contained about six pints. The <hi type="italic">shekel</hi> is here settled (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.13">v. 13</reference>); it is twenty <hi type="italic">jerahs,</hi> just half a <hi type="italic">Roman</hi> ounce, in our money 2<hi type="italic">s.</hi> 4 1/4<hi type="italic">d.</hi> and almost the eighth part of a farthing, as the aforesaid learned man exactly computes it. By the shekels the <hi type="italic">maneh,</hi> or pound, was reckoned, which, when it was set for a mere weight (says bishop Cumberland), without respect to coinage, contained just 100 shekels, as appears by comparing <reference osisRef="1Kgs.10.17">1 Kings x. 17</reference>, where it is said three <hi type="italic">manehs,</hi> or <hi type="italic">pounds, of gold, went to one shield,</hi> with the parallel place, <reference osisRef="2Chr.9.16">2 Chron. ix. 16</reference>, where it is said 300 <hi type="italic">shekels of gold went to one shield.</hi> But when the <hi type="italic">maneh</hi> is set for a sum of money or coin it contains but sixty shekels, as appears here, where twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels, and fifteen shekels, which in all make sixty, shall be the <hi type="italic">maneh.</hi> But it is thus reckoned because they had one piece of money that weighed twenty shekels, another twenty-five, another fifteen, all of which made up one pound, as a learned writer here observes. Note, It concerns God's Israel to be very honest and just in all their dealings, very punctual and exact in rendering to all their due, and very cautious to do wrong to none, because otherwise they spoil the acceptableness of their profession with God and the reputation of it before men.
entries.d736c7393cb8a08fc2f8e291f01494db76433e30: <div eID="gen19269" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">Oblations Enjoined. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 574.)</title> <div sID="gen19270" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">13</hi> This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the oblation that ye shall offer; the sixth part of an ephah of a homer of wheat, and ye shall give the sixth part of an ephah of a homer of barley: <hi type="super">14</hi> Concerning the ordinance of oil, the bath of oil, <hi type="italic">ye shall offer</hi> the tenth part of a bath out of the cor, <hi type="italic">which is</hi> an homer of ten baths; for ten baths <hi type="italic">are</hi> a homer: <hi type="super">15</hi> And one lamb out of the flock, out of two hundred, out of the fat pastures of Israel; for a meat offering, and for a burnt offering, and for peace offerings, to make reconciliation for them, saith the Lord <hi type="small-caps">God</hi> . <hi type="super">16</hi> All the people of the land shall give this oblation for the prince in Israel. <hi type="super">17</hi> And it shall be the prince's part <hi type="italic">to give</hi> burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and drink offerings, in the feasts, and in the new moons, and in the sabbaths, in all solemnities of the house of Israel: he shall prepare the sin offering, and the meat offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel. <hi type="super">18</hi> Thus saith the Lord <hi type="small-caps">God</hi> ; In the first <hi type="italic">month,</hi> in the first <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the month, thou shalt take a young bullock without blemish, and cleanse the sanctuary: <hi type="super">19</hi> And the priest shall take of the blood of the sin offering, and put <hi type="italic">it</hi> upon the posts of the house, and upon the four corners of the settle of the altar, and upon the posts of the gate of the inner court. <hi type="super">20</hi> And so thou shalt do the seventh <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the month for every one that erreth, and for <hi type="italic">him that is</hi> simple: so shall ye reconcile the house. <hi type="super">21</hi> In the first <hi type="italic">month,</hi> in the fourteenth day of the month, ye shall have the passover, a feast of seven days; unleavened bread shall be eaten. <hi type="super">22</hi> And upon that day shall the prince prepare for himself and for all the people of the land a bullock <hi type="italic">for</hi> a sin offering. <hi type="super">23</hi> And seven days of the feast he shall prepare a burnt offering to the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , seven bullocks and seven rams without blemish daily the seven days; and a kid of the goats daily <hi type="italic">for</hi> a sin offering. <hi type="super">24</hi> And he shall prepare a meat offering of an ephah for a bullock, and an ephah for a ram, and a hin of oil for an ephah. <hi type="super">25</hi> In the seventh <hi type="italic">month,</hi> in the fifteenth day of the month, shall he do the like in the feast of the seven days, according to the sin offering, according to the burnt offering, and according to the meat offering, and according to the oil. <div eID="gen19270" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19271" type="x-p"/> Having laid down the rules of the righteousness toward men, which is really a branch off true religion, he comes next to give some directions for their religion towards God, which is a branch of universal righteousness. <div eID="gen19271" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19272" type="x-p"/> I. It is required that they offer an oblation to the Lord out of what they have (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.13">v. 13</reference>): <hi type="italic">All the people of the land</hi> must give an oblation, <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.16">v. 16</reference>. As God's tenants, they must pay a quitrent to their great landlord. They had offered an oblation out of their real estates (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.1">v. 1</reference>), a <hi type="italic">holy portion of their land;</hi> now they are directed to offer an oblation out of their personal estates, their goods and chattels, as an acknowledgement of their receivings from him, their dependence on him, and their obligations to him. Note, Whatever our substance is we must honour God with it, by giving him his dues out of it. Not that God has need of or may be benefited by any thing that we can give him, <reference osisRef="Ps.50.9">Ps. l. 9</reference>. No; it is but an <hi type="italic">oblation;</hi> we only <hi type="italic">offer it</hi> to him; the benefit of it returns back to ourselves, to his poor, who, as our neighbours, are ourselves, or to his ministers who serve continually for our good. <div eID="gen19272" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19273" type="x-p"/> II. The proportion of this oblation is here determined, which was not done by the law of Moses. No mention is made of the title, but only of this oblation. And the <hi type="italic">quantum</hi> of this is thus settled:—1. Out of their corn they were to offer a sixtieth part; out of every <hi type="italic">homer of wheat and barley,</hi> which contained ten ephahs, they were to offer the sixth part of one ephah, which was a sixtieth part of the whole, <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.13">v. 13</reference>. 2. Out of their oil (and probably their wine too) they were to offer a hundredth part, for this oblation; out of every cor, or homer, which contained ten baths they were to offer the tenth part of one bath, <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.14">v. 14</reference>. This was given to the altar; for in every meat-offering there was <hi type="italic">flour mingled with oil.</hi> 3. Out of their flocks they were to give <hi type="italic">one lamb</hi> out of 200; that was the smallest proportion of all, <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.15">v. 15</reference>. But it must be <hi type="italic">out of the fat pastures of Israel.</hi> They must not offer to God that which was taken up from the common, but the fattest and best they had, for <hi type="italic">burnt-offerings</hi> and <hi type="italic">peace-offerings:</hi> the former were offered for the giving of glory to God, the latter for the fetching in of mercy, grace, and peace, from God, and in our spiritual sacrifices these are our two great errands at the throne of grace; but, in order to the acceptance of both, these sacrifices were to <hi type="italic">make reconciliation</hi> for them. Christ is our sacrifice of atonement, by whom reconciliation is made, and to him we must have an eye in our sacrifices of acknowledgment. <div eID="gen19273" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19274" type="x-p"/> III. This oblation must be given <hi type="italic">for the prince in Israel,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.16">v. 16</reference>. Some read it <hi type="italic">to</hi> the prince, and understand it of Christ, who is indeed the prince in Israel, to whom we must offer our oblations, and into whose hands we must put them, to be presented to the Father. Or, They shall give it <hi type="italic">with</hi> the prince; every private person shall bring his oblation, to be offered with that of the prince; for it follows (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.17">v. 17</reference>). It <hi type="italic">shall be the prince's part to provide</hi> all the offerings, <hi type="italic">to make reconciliation for the house of Israel.</hi> The people were to bring their oblations to him according to the foregoing rules, and he was to bring them to the sanctuary, and to make up what fell short out of his own. Note, It is the duty of rulers to take care of religion, and to see that the duties of it be regularly and carefully performed by those under their charge, and that nothing be wanting that is requisite thereto: the magistrate is the keeper of both tables; and it is a happy thing when those that are above others in power and dignity go before them in the service of God. <div eID="gen19274" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19275" type="x-p"/> IV. Some particular solemnities are here appointed. <div eID="gen19275" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19276" type="x-p"/> 1. Here is one in the beginning of the year, which seems to be altogether new, and not instituted by the law of Moses; it is the annual solemnity of cleansing the sanctuary. (1.) <hi type="italic">On the first day of the first month</hi> (upon new-year's day) they were to offer a sacrifice for the <hi type="italic">cleansing of the sanctuary</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.18">v. 18</reference>), that is, to make atonement for the iniquity of the holy things the year past, that they might bring none of the guilt of them into the services of the new year, and to implore grace for the preventing of that iniquity, and for the better performance of the service of the sanctuary the ensuing year. And, in token of this, the blood of this <hi type="italic">sin-offering</hi> was to be put upon the <hi type="italic">posts of the gate of the inner court</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.19">v. 19</reference>), to signify that by it atonement was intended to be made for the sins of all the servants that attended that house, priests, Levites, and people, even the sins that were found in all their services. Note, Even sanctuaries on earth need cleansing, frequent cleansing; that above needs none. Those what worship God together should often join in renewing their repentance for their manifold defects, and applying the blood of Christ for the pardon of them, and in renewing their covenants to be more careful for the future; and it is very seasonable to begin the year with this work, as Hezekiah did when it had been long neglected, <reference osisRef="1Chr.29.17">2 Chron. xxix. 17</reference>. They were here appointed to <hi type="italic">cleanse the sanctuary</hi> upon the first day of the month, because on the fourteenth day of the month they were to eat the <hi type="italic">passover,</hi> an ordinance which, of all Old-Testament institutions, had most in it of Christ and gospel grace, and therefore it was very fit that they should begin to prepare for it a fortnight before by cleansing the sanctuary. (2.) This sacrifice was to be repeated <hi type="italic">on the seventh day of the first month,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.20">v. 20</reference>. And then it was intended to make atonement <hi type="italic">for every one that errs, and for him that is simple.</hi> Note, He that sins <hi type="italic">errs and is simple;</hi> he mistakes, he goes out of the way, and shows himself to be foolish and unwise. But here it is spoken of those sins which are committed through ignorance, mistake, or inadvertency, whether by any of the priests, or of the Levites, or of the people. Sacrifices were appointed to atone for such sins as men were surprised into, or did before they were aware, which they would not have done if they had known and remembered aright, which they were overtaken in, and for which, afterwards, they condemn themselves. But for presumptuous sins, committed with a high hand, there was no sacrifice appointed, <reference osisRef="Num.15.30">Num. xv. 30</reference>. By these repeated sacrifices you shall <hi type="italic">reconcile the house,</hi> that is, God will be reconciled to it, and continue the tokens of his presence in it, and will <hi type="italic">let it alone this year also.</hi> <div eID="gen19276" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19277" type="x-p"/> 2. The passover was to be religiously observed at the time appointed, <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.21">v. 21</reference>. Christ is <hi type="italic">our passover,</hi> that is <hi type="italic">sacrificed for us.</hi> We celebrate the memorial of that sacrifice and feast upon it, triumphing in our deliverance out of the Egyptian slavery of sin and our preservation from the sword of the destroying angel, the sword of divine justice, in the Lord's supper, which is our passover-feast, as the whole Christian life is, and must be, the feast of unleavened bread. It is here appointed that the prince shall prepare a <hi type="italic">sin-offering,</hi> to be offered <hi type="italic">for himself and the people,</hi> a bullock on the <hi type="italic">first</hi> day (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.22">v. 22</reference>) and a <hi type="italic">kid of the goats</hi> every other day (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.23">v. 23</reference>), to teach us, in all our attendance upon God for communion with him, to have an eye to the great sin-offering, by which <hi type="italic">transgression</hi> was <hi type="italic">finished</hi> and an <hi type="italic">everlasting righteousness brought in.</hi> On every day of the feast there was to be a <hi type="italic">burnt-offering,</hi> purely for the honour of God, of no less than seven bullocks and seven rams, with their meat-offering, which were wholly consumed upon the altar, and yet <hi type="italic">no waste,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.23-Ezek.45.24">v. 23, 24</reference>. <div eID="gen19277" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19278" type="x-p"/> 3. The feast of tabernacles; that is spoken of next (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.25">v. 25</reference>), and there is no mention of the feast of pentecost, which came between that of the passover and that of tabernacles. Orders are here given (above what were given by the law of Moses) for the same sacrifices to be offered during the seven days of the passover. See the deficiency of the legal sacrifices for sin; they were therefore often repeated, not only every year, but every feast, every day of the feast, because <hi type="italic">they could not make the comers thereunto perfect,</hi> <reference osisRef="Heb.10.1">Heb. x. 1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Heb.10.3">3</reference>. See the necessity of our frequently repeating the same religious exercises. Though the sacrifice of atonement is offered <hi type="italic">once for all,</hi> yet the sacrifices of acknowledgement, that of a broken heart, that of a thankful heart, those spiritual sacrifices which are acceptable to God through Christ Jesus, must be every day offered. We should, as here, fall into a method of holy duties, and keep to it.  <chapter eID="Ezek.45"/> <div eID="gen19278" type="x-p"/>

entries.51eb531cfed9098c2dce242aeebe90433215dd1d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11883"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 45</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ezek.45.1-Ezek.45.25">Eze 45:1-25</reference>. Allotment of the Land for the Sanctuary, the City, and the Prince.</title> <div sID="gen21476" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11883"/><hi type="bold">1. offer an oblation--</hi>from a Hebrew root to "heave" or "raise"; when anything was offered to God, the offerer raised the hand. The special territorial division for the tribes is given in the forty-seventh and forty-eighth chapters. Only Jehovah's portion is here subdivided into its three parts: (1) that for the sanctuary (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.2">Eze 45:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.3">3</reference>); (2) that for the priests (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.4">Eze 45:4</reference>); (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.3">3</reference>) that for the Levites (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.5">Eze 45:5</reference>). Compare <reference osisRef="Ezek.48.8-Ezek.48.13">Eze 48:8-13</reference>.<div eID="gen21476" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21477" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">five and twenty thousand reeds, &c.--</hi>So English Version rightly fills the ellipsis (compare Note, see on <reference osisRef="Ezek.42.16">Eze 42:16</reference>). Hence "cubits" are mentioned in <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.2">Eze 45:2</reference>, not here, implying that there alone cubits are meant. Taking each reed at twelve feet, the area of the whole would be a square of sixty miles on each side. The whole forming a square betokens the settled stability of the community and the harmony of all classes. "An holy portion of the land" (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.1">Eze 45:1</reference>) comprised the whole length, and only two-fifths of the breadth. The outer territory in its distribution harmonizes with the inner and more sacred arrangements of the sanctuary. No room is to be given for oppression (see <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.8">Eze 45:8</reference>), all having ample provision made for their wants and comforts. All will mutually co-operate without constraint or contention. <div eID="gen21477" type="x-p"/>
entries.54d40a90f7ac250b6867079838728510e49314dc: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11884"/><div sID="gen21478" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11884"/>7. The prince's possession is to consist of two halves, one on the west, the other on the east, of the sacred territory. The prince, as head of the holy community, stands in closest connection with the sanctuary; his possession, therefore, on both sides must adjoin that which was peculiarly the Lord's [Fairbairn]. <div eID="gen21478" type="x-p"/>
entries.04a55c44876dd0d7c7656098dc1e920ad4b0cc5a: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11885"/><div sID="gen21479" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11885"/>12. The standard weights were lost when the Chaldeans destroyed the temple. The threefold enumeration of shekels (twenty, twenty-five, fifteen) probably refers to coins of different value, representing respectively so many shekels, the three collectively making up a maneh. By weighing these together against the maneh, a test was afforded whether they severally had their proper weight: sixty shekels in all, containing one coin a fourth of the whole (fifteen shekels), another a third (twenty shekels), another a third and a twelfth (twenty-five shekels) [Menochius]. The Septuagint reads, "fifty shekels shall be your maneh." <div eID="gen21479" type="x-p"/>
entries.11adcf15dfb9690d5e3c3445836cdac33c39c65d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11886"/><div sID="gen21480" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11886"/>13-15. In these oblations there is a progression as to the relation between the kind and the quantity: of the corn, the sixth of a tenth, that is, a sixtieth part of the quantity specified; of the oil, the tenth of a tenth, that is, an hundredth part; and of the flock, one from every two hundred. <div eID="gen21480" type="x-p"/>
entries.014a2233893891ad4deb299c9eb3efdbc1610bd1: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11887"/><div sID="gen21481" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11887"/>18. The year is to begin with a consecration service, not mentioned under the Levitical law; but an earnest of it is given in the feast of dedication of the second temple, which celebrated its purification by Judas Maccabeus, after its defilement by Antiochus. <div eID="gen21481" type="x-p"/>
entries.4ed80a967a3f9749381cf22ed5470ca6b7c478fc: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11888"/><div sID="gen21482" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11888"/><hi type="bold">20. for him that is simple--</hi>for sins of ignorance (<reference osisRef="Lev.4.2">Le 4:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.13.27">13, 27</reference>). <div eID="gen21482" type="x-p"/>
entries.fd9ae62860e819fb145d9cac4dcca0d093b93c29: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11889"/><div sID="gen21483" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11889"/>21. As a new solemnity, the feast of consecration is to prepare for the passover; so the passover itself is to have different sacrifices from those of the Mosaic law. Instead of one ram and seven lambs for the daily burnt offering, there are to be seven bullocks and seven rams. So also whereas the feast of tabernacles had its own offerings, which diminished as the days of the feast advanced, here the same are appointed as on the passover. Thus it is implied that the letter of the law is to give place to its spirit, those outward rites of Judaism having no intrinsic efficacy, but symbolizing the spiritual truths of Messiah's kingdom, as for instance the perfect holiness which is to characterize it. Compare <reference osisRef="1Cor.5.7">1Co 5:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.5.8">8</reference>, as to our spiritual "passover," wherein, at the Lord's supper, we feed on Christ by faith, accompanied with "the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth." Literal ordinances, though not slavishly bound to the letter of the law, will set forth the catholic and eternal verities of Messiah's kingdom. <chapter eID="Ezek.45"/>

entries.88196c8ee1636e28c26c23d82f3cdde5fa328dd9: <div eID="gen32574" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen32575" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen32576" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen32576" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen32575" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen32577" type="x-p"/> The several portions of land appointed for the sanctuary, <reference osisRef="Eze.45.1-Eze.45.5">Eze 45:1-5</reference>, the city, 6, and the prince, <reference osisRef="Eze.45.7">Eze 45:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Eze.45.8">Eze 45:8</reference>. Regulations concerning the weights and measures, <reference osisRef="Eze.45.9-Eze.45.12">Eze 45:9-12</reference>; with ordinances respecting the provisions for the ordinary and extraordinary sacrifices, <reference osisRef="Eze.45.13-Eze.45.25">Eze 45:13-25</reference>. <div eID="gen32577" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32578" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen32578" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32579" type="x-p"/> When ye shall divide by lot - That is, when on your repossessing your land, every family settles according to the allotment which they formerly had; for it is certain that the land was not divided afresh by lot after the Babylonish captivity. The allotment mentioned and described here was merely for the service of the temple, the use of the priests, and the prince or governor of the people. A division of the whole land is not intended.

entries.f0bc2e60fdfbce0608c31579e327c04e1f3d9f2e: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen32582" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32583" type="x-p"/> And the five and twenty thousand - See the plan, B.
entries.0011606844976a047977a3cd893b15243402cad1: <hi type="bold">Verse 6</hi> <div eID="gen32583" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32584" type="x-p"/> Ye shall appoint - See the plan, FF.
entries.2af32a8be57c5e57728495fbffc97bfcef63328c: <hi type="bold">Verse 7</hi> <div eID="gen32584" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32585" type="x-p"/> A portion shall be for the prince - נשיא nasi, he who had the authority of chief magistrate; for there was neither king nor prince among the Jews after the Babylonish captivity. For these allotments and divisions, see the plan, EE, FF, GG.
entries.fd2377ca0db76b7a964484a3ed345e7676a46f5f: <hi type="bold">Verse 8</hi> <div eID="gen32585" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32586" type="x-p"/> My princes shall no more oppress my people - By exorbitant taxes to maintain profligate courts, or subsidize other powers to help to keep up a system of tyranny in the earth. The former princes even robbed the temple of God to give subsidies to other states.
entries.a034d9a76447b9d16d5010ece30f51cc2f38b616: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen32586" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32587" type="x-p"/> Take away your exactions from my people - This is the voice of God to all the rulers of the earth. <div eID="gen32587" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32588" type="x-p"/> Take away your exactions; do not oppress the people; they are mine. Abolish all oppressive taxes.
entries.30b49fca694d599709e12311f9320dbf42ba7825: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen32588" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32589" type="x-p"/> Ye shall have just balances - This appreciation of weights, measures, and money was intended to show them that they must not introduce those to which they had been accustomed in the captivity, but those which God had prescribed to their forefathers. entries.a2ec6b0d9b251af200677f349e5794ba181771eb: <hi type="bold">Verse 18</hi> <div eID="gen32590" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32591" type="x-p"/> Thou shalt take a young bullock - and cleanse the sanctuary - There is nothing of this in the Mosaic law; it seems to have been a new ceremony. entries.6a1533854ff70216b7d8d091530688e521508023: <hi type="bold">Verse 20</hi> <div eID="gen32591" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32592" type="x-p"/> For him that is simple - That wants understanding to conduct himself properly.
entries.d2eb356239241168d6d3c8120d9e13718046a133: <hi type="bold">Verse 25</hi> <div eID="gen32592" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32593" type="x-p"/> In the seventh month - He shall do at the feast of tabernacles the same things that he was desired to do on the passover. The prince should offer the same number of victims, of the same quality, and with the same ceremonies, as during the above seven days.
